Following the Senior Race on the 12th December,the Juniors turned out to compete for the Savage Shield on December 19th and it was only to be expected that Ron Linstead who was 2nd in the Snior Championship, should prove the winner.

We need some new blood so before April let us see some form from such people as Miller, Thresher, Linstead, Johnston, Stearman, and a return to the team by Hallowell, Davies and Baulch (not new blood but almost indispensable).
Kerr, Newell, Davies, Walker, Black, Dabbs, Linstead, Maclean. How's that for a line up to set a new 3 mile record?

Our turnout for this fixture against Mitcham A.C. and Croydon H. was most disappointing for, besides having a team performing in the Hogs Back race, we were also without the services of Kerr, Dabbs, and Linstead who were unfortunately unavailable.
Belgrave were without Sawyer and Linstead, but Denis Jones ran very well and with the support of Norman Stairs and Len Bishop, we were placed third.

CENTRE LEFT: Linstead, the holder, leads Newell and Black in the Club 10 miles Championship for the "Macher" shield. CENTRE RIGHT: Walker, Black, Sawyer, Thresher and North head the field at 2½ miles in the Club 7 miles 6hampionship for the "Blackstaffe" shield.

On paper we had high hopes of being second to Portsmouth AC but once again we were unable to field a truly representative team and the ten that did start were dogged by misfortune.Those that were unable to appear were Linstead (injury), Thresher (cold), Newell (work) and Roffey (flu).

Yet during our recent lean years, the name of Pat Newell has figured consistently and he has, along with other stalwarts like Walker, Linstead, Dabbs, Davies and Maclean, Helped keep the Belgrave flag flying, albeit a little limply.
Kerr, Linstead and Dear were capable of causing some upsets. The biggest surprise though, in the end, was Geoff's state of fitness which gave him the slowest time in our 'A' and 'B' teams.
Ranjit finds thirst to be more of a problem than fatigue. Funny---so do Don Maclean and Linstead!
